solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ambitious Democrat torn apart

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat
riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A political observer describes a Democrat being savaged by rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driven is strongly motivated to succeed, which is a synonym for ambitious.

clue.text: Forsaken by the German priest at court

parts.note: der is a German word for the
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Abandoned by a German cleric in a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at court' looks like a place, but 'at' just joins and court is the abbreviation CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict means abandoned and left to decay, a synonym of forsaken.

clue.text: Usually finding popular fellow artist by lake

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Gene is a man's name, so any fellow
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: As a rule a well-liked man paints beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a man's name for 'fellow' is loose but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means as a rule or for the most part, which is what usually means.

clue.text: Created set-up to produce kind of mild cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: made means created

explanation.surface: A dairy operation was established to make a gentle cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Enthusiasts collecting reportedly scanty things causing annoyance

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: people bitten by the bug are enthusiasts; BUG is placed around the next piece and S closes it

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym rather than is spelt like it

parts.note: scanty means bare, and bare sounds like the animal

explanation.surface: Fans gathering skimpy items, presumably to their own irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scanty' looks like it describes the things, but it is the sound-alike piece set inside the enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of irritation, so bugbears are things that annoy.

clue.text: Puts into service to accommodate the French poor

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house or take in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: uses means puts into service
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: Someone employs French paupers, a charitable gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor in the sense of inadequate or ineffective work means useless.

clue.text: In the process of lining brakes he designed for a bike

indicators.note: lining means forming the inside layer, so the small word goes within the rearranged letters
designed means newly put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
on, as in on the go, means in the process of

explanation.surface: An inventor fits brake linings on a bicycle he has designed.
explanation.walkthrough: ON goes inside the rearranged letters of brakes he, after the first B.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneshaker is an early bicycle with solid tyres, nicknamed for its rough ride.

clue.text: Trouble in the past overwhelming King George

indicators.note: overwhelming suggests swamping or engulfing, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A historical uprising that overpowered a Georgian monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British for aggressive trouble or hassle, a synonym of trouble.

clue.text: Concerned primarily about space at back of bus shelter

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter

indicators.note: back of means only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its first letter
re means about or concerning
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Worried mainly about room at the rear of a bus stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The C-RE-EN chain is placed at the back of S, the last letter of bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen shields or protects something, so as a noun or verb it means shelter.

clue.text: Certain to need small springs

parts.note: bound, as in bound to happen, means certain
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A mechanic is sure a device will want little coils.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounds as a verb means leaps, and springs as a verb also means leaps.

clue.text: Girl more worried about American's garbled nonsense

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation
worried in the sense of tugged and pulled about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A girl grows anxious over an American's confused ramblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the American abbreviation within the rearranged letters rather than around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, rambling, confused account, which is a garbled nonsense of talk.

clue.text: Runner from Northern Ireland for example turned right

parts.note: NI is the standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland

indicators.note: turned means faced the other way, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An athlete from Belfast, say, swings round to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' wants to be an athlete; in crosswords it often means a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a major West African river, and rivers run, so a crossword runner is a river.

clue.text: Bonds, by the sound of it, with cat

indicators.note: by the sound of it says to go by pronunciation, not spelling

parts.note: bonds are links, which is pronounced like the wild cat's name

explanation.surface: Someone describes ties of affection with a pet, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild member of the cat family with tufted ears.

clue.text: Less than successful attempt to get drugs causes stress

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
in slang, to score is to manage to buy illegal drugs

explanation.surface: A failed bid to buy narcotics leads to anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than successful' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Less than' is one piece and 'successful attempt to get drugs' is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore a point is to emphasise it, so the verb is a synonym of stress.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of brain injury has hint of encouragement for you they say

indicators.note: has, read as takes in place of, swaps one letter in the injury word for another

parts.note: a blow to the head causing temporary loss of function

indicators.note: hint of means only a trace, the first letter, is kept

parts.note: its first letter

indicators.note: they say means as spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: the letter name sounds like the pronoun

explanation.surface: Recognition that a head injury was helped by a little encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: In the injury word, E replaces the U that sounds like you.
explanation.definitionFit: A concession is an admission that a point is valid, a kind of acknowledgement.

clue.text: Eager to know rule on copper with debts

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the rule piece follows the metal piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is an abbreviation for rule
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A regulation about a police officer who owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is also slang for a police officer, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curious means wanting to find things out, a synonym of eager to know.

clue.text: Handles sent back without first class rating

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the word is read right to left
without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed word goes around the letter

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
A is the top grade, first class

explanation.surface: Door handles get returned because they are not top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside: SEMAN goes around A. A rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the navy a rating is an enlisted sailor, and a seaman is one such sailor.

clue.text: Clumsy bishop entering small hut stumbles

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the abbreviation joins the letters of the other words
stumbles suggests tripping and falling about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An awkward cleric trips over as he goes into a tiny shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all thumbs is an idiom for having awkward hands, i.e. being clumsy.

clue.text: Prediction of support finds His Excellency extremely coy

parts.note: a prop is a support
HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so just the two end letters are taken

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A forecast of backing finds an ambassador very bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophecy is a foretelling of the future, which is a prediction.

clue.text: Bring to light letters from Felicity

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters taken out of the next word

parts.note: the run sits inside the name

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have Felicity's correspondence made public.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or evoke a response or fact, i.e. bring it to light.

clue.text: Tread on tyre? Oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd positions only, first and third

parts.note: its first and third letters
ample means enough or plenty

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about stepping on a car tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' reads as a single phrase meaning strangely, but it splits: 'Oddly' acts on tyre and 'enough' is a piece of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to crush something underfoot, which is treading on it heavily.

clue.text: Sell rat out? Excellent

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An approving cry at the idea of betraying a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar, literally of the stars, is used informally to mean outstanding or exceptionally good.

clue.text: First of toddies in golf club is precisely what's required

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for the golf club

parts.note: a spoon is an old-fashioned lofted wooden golf club

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A first round of hot drinks at the golf club hits the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water and sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is British informal for exactly right, i.e. precisely what is wanted.

clue.text: Spy taking in soldiers' spirit of optimism

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing within, so the spy word goes round the soldiers

parts.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation
RA, the Royal Artillery, is a British army regiment

explanation.surface: An agent who absorbs the troops' upbeat mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers' spirit' wants to be one phrase, but the possessive belongs to the RA piece and 'spirit of optimism' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and enthusiasm of a group, its spirit of optimism.

clue.text: Render insignificant during performance outside today

parts.note: over can mean during, as in over the weekend

indicators.note: outside means wrapped round, so the word for performance encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a show is a performance
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A director's note about making something seem trivial in a modern staging.
explanation.walkthrough: AD for 'today' is a stretch: it is the current era.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow something is to make it seem less important by comparison.

clue.text: Particular force

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to demand or extract by pressure

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means precise, as a verb it means to extract by insistence, like forcing payment.

clue.text: Steal instrument of punishment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slang verb for pinch or nick
second meaning: a lash used for flogging

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with a flogging device.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for stealing quickly, and also names a lash for beating.

clue.text: Spoken for female ignored Capone

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A woman was taken by a gangster, it was said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but is the source: FOR loses F to leave OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Mites found in Madeira cake on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling backwards, so the run reads right to left
found in means sitting within the following words

parts.note: the run spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Tiny insects turn up in a slice of sponge on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeira cake is a plain British sponge cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Acari is the scientific name for mites and ticks, as a plural of acarus.

clue.text: In favour of having little weight attached to Peto's plan of action

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a gram is a small unit of weight
the setter, Peto, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter endorses a scheme involving a slight load.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a planned series of steps or activities, i.e. a plan of action.

clue.text: Was conducive with former partner stretched out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tended, as in tended to produce, means was conducive

explanation.surface: Something helped along by an ex was drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means lengthened or prolonged, a synonym of stretched out.

clue.text: Elegant form on end of quay

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A school group stands smartly at the edge of the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy is an informal word for stylish or sophisticated, i.e. elegant.
